newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia kicks off ZCCM privatisation with first sale.
newsitem.headline: Zambia kicks off ZCCM privatisation with first sale.

text.p: Zambia kicked off the privatisation of its biggest state-owned company on Thursday with the sale of one of the copper mines of Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines Ltd (ZCCM).
ZCCM said in a statement it had agreed to sell 80 percent of the Kansanshi copper mine to the U.S.-based Cyprus Amax Minerals Company for an undisclosed figure.
Kansanshi is the first ZCCM mine to be sold under Zambia's ambitious programme to privatisate state assets.

"The chairman of ZCCM, Luke Mwananshiku, today signed an agreement providing for Cyprus Amax Minerals Company to eventually acquire an 80 percent interest in ZCCM's Kansanshi copper mine and deposit," a ZCCM statement said.
Kansanshi has a resource base of 24.4 million tonnes of ore at 2.9 percent copper content and has been operated on a limited scale by ZCCM.
Cyprus Amax -- based in Colorado -- is a leading copper and coal producer and is exploring for base and precious metals worldwide.
Mwananshiku said in the statement he was pleased that the sale agreements for Kansanshi had been successfully executed.

But he said the sale of Kansanshi helped little with ZCCM's pressing financial difficulities and stressed the need for the sale of the company's main operating mines, smelters and power infrastructure.

"There is no disguising ZCCM's serious and immediate financial problems. The fall in the copper price and ZCCM's inability to borrow long-term mean that the company's liquidity is being severely squeezed.
"It is therefore imperative that the sale of the rest of ZCCM's assets continue uninterrupted," Mwananshiku said.
Analysts believe that ZCCM's earnings have fallen 33 percent in the past year compared to 1995.
Zambia's privatisation programme is regarded by some economic analysts as Africa's most successful, with the sale of 130 state firms in four years.
Zambia Privatisation Agency chief Valentine Chitalu told reporters this week that the agency expected to conclude the privatisation of ZCCM by the end of 1998.
ZCCM assets have been split into different packages for privatisation.
The privatisation of ZCCM, which earns around 90 percent of the country's foreign exchange earnings, is seen as crucial to the survival of Zambia's mining industry.
